today.text: The Wang Fuk Court fire, a catastrophic fire in Tai Po, Hong Kong, leaves at least 168 dead and 79 injured.
COVID-19 pandemic: The World Health Organization identifies the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

A magnitude 6.4 earthquake strikes western Albania leaving at least 52 people dead and over 1,000 injured. This was the world's deadliest earthquake of 2019, and the deadliest to strike the country in 99 years.
The robotic probe Insight lands on Elysium Planitia, Mars.
NATO attack in Pakistan: NATO forces in Afghanistan attack a Pakistani check post in a friendly fire incident, killing 24 soldiers and wounding 13 others.
The Mars Science Laboratory launches to Mars with the Curiosity Rover.
Mumbai attacks, a series of coordinated terrorist attacks took place in Mumbai killing 166 citizens by 10 terrorists of Lashkar-e-Taiba, a Pakistan based extremist Islamist terrorist organisation.
The ocean liner Queen Elizabeth 2, now out of service, docks in Dubai.
Ruzhou School massacre: A man stabs and kills eight people and seriously wounds another four in a school dormitory in Ruzhou, China.
The last Poʻouli (Black-faced honeycreeper) dies of avian malaria in the Maui Bird Conservation Center in Olinda, Hawaii, before it could breed, making the species in all probability extinct.

random.title: Ba'ath Brigades
random.extract: The Ba'ath Brigades (Arabic: كتائب البعث, romanized: Katā'ib al-Baʿth), also known as the Ba'ath Battalions, were a Syrian volunteer militia made up of Syrian Ba'ath Party members, almost entirely of Sunni Muslims from Syria and many Arab countries, loyal to the Ba'athist-led regime in power at the time.

entry.title: Eye in the Sky: The Milky Way over Lençóis
entry.summary:
Explanation: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder. And there is much to behold in today's featured image. The Milky Way shines bright in the sky of Brazil, over the white sand dunes and dark lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park. We can see different parts of the Milky Way as it apparently rotates in the sky every night and throughout the year. This composite image was taken later in the night in July from a latitude of approximately 2º south. It shows some prominent Milky Way features, such as dark dust lanes and colorful nebulas. But does the Galaxy really appear arched like a rainbow in the sky? No, this is an artifact of a picture taken with a wide-angle lens. As the Galaxy was artfully framed by the photographer, it matches the contour of the dark lagoon creating the illusion of a cosmic eye, half in space and half on the ground. Is this eye in the sky looking back at you?

Tomorrow's picture: what's next?
